body.condition: The law \(P\) of \(X\) is jointly centered Gaussian.

novel.justification: Joint Gaussianity is an explicitly restrictive component of the maintained covariance-based subclass. It makes the observed second moments determine the maintained law and makes zero cross-covariance equivalent to independence of the coordinate disturbance stacks. It is plausible for coordinate-aligned repeated measurements with Gaussian shared shocks and readout noise, but excludes the broader non-Gaussian LiMVAM families used by several comparators.
